note: The wire schema of `.loomux/workflow.yml`, as data (#880 slice A).
This file IS the contract, not a description of one. Two tests enforce it, one per side:
compares every section below, key for key, against what the engine's `Raw*` serde
mirrors actually accept (`workflow::workflow_schema_keys()`). A field added to or
removed from a `Raw*` struct without editing this file is a RED test, not a silent
- test/workflowschema.test.ts asserts the pane's own model round-trips every field
below (the parser knows it — it never lands in `extra`; the canonical serializer
emits it), and tracks which fields still have no editor.
It describes loomux's OWN product schema — the shape of a workflow file, never any
particular repo's roster (CLAUDE.md constraint 8). `blocks:` is data; what is pinned
here is what a block IS.
Adding a field: add it to the engine's `Raw*` struct, to this manifest, to the pane's
model (`src/workflowmodel.ts` — KNOWN_* + the emitters), and to a form descriptor. The
tests refuse to let you stop after the first step.

types.multiline: free text over many lines (emitted as a YAML block scalar)
types.number: an integer; `min`/`max` state the engine's own bounds where it has any
types.enum: one of `values` — a closed set this build refuses to go outside of
types.path: a repo-relative file path (never absolute, never escaping the repo)
types.block-ref: the `id` of a block declared in this same file
types.section: a nested mapping whose shape is the section named in `section`
types.section-map: a mapping of author-chosen names to `section` mappings

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.help: The top level of the file: what this workflow is called, and the sections it declares.

fields.name: version
fields.help: The schema version this file speaks. This build reads and writes version 1; anything else is refused rather than guessed at.

fields.name: name
fields.help: Display name for the workflow. Cosmetic — nothing references it.

fields.name: authored_with
fields.help: The loomux version that CREATED the file. Informational, never a validation error, and never restamped on save — it records who authored the workflow, not who last looked at it.

fields.name: blocks
fields.help: The agents a run may use. Order matters: the first block of a capability class is what an unrouted spawn of that class resolves to.

fields.name: edges
fields.help: The declared happy path. ADVISORY — the orchestrator still decides when to spawn what.

fields.name: gates
fields.help: What must be true before a merge. ENFORCED in the `gh` PATH shim, not in a prompt. Keyed by gate name; today the only gate is `merge`.

fields.name: intake
fields.help: Where autonomous work comes from, and what its label vocabulary is called. Absent = loomux's built-in profile.

fields.name: merge_queue
fields.help: Policy for the bisecting merge queue on orchestrator-owned integration branches. Absent = off, and behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

fields.name: resources
fields.help: Named lock resources agents may acquire, keyed by a name this repo chooses (loomux never learns what it means). Absent = the lock tools are not offered at all.

block.title: Block
block.help: One agent: who it is, what capability class it runs as, and what it runs on.

fields.name: id
fields.help: Immutable identity — edges and gates name THIS, never the display name. Lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_'.

fields.name: name
fields.help: Display label. Renaming it can never break a reference; that is its whole point.

fields.name: kind
fields.help: The capability class. CLOSED: a workflow file may define any persona, but it can never invent a capability.

fields.name: cli
fields.help: The agent CLI this block spawns on. Empty inherits the group's CLI.

fields.name: model
fields.help: The model to pin for this block. Empty = the CLI's own default.

fields.name: prompt
fields.help: Inline persona, compiled to the CLI's native inline-agent flag. Mutually exclusive with `profile`.

fields.name: profile
fields.help: Persona FILE, repo-relative (e.g. .github/agents/worker.md). Mutually exclusive with `prompt`.

fields.name: allow
fields.help: Extra pre-approved tool patterns, e.g. "Bash(gh pr view --json title,body)". Refused on a read-only kind, and it can never re-grant a denied tool — deny beats allow on every CLI.

fields.name: role_hint
fields.help: An INERT persona/template marker — never a capability. `advisor` requires kind: planner, `process` requires kind: worker.

fields.name: effort
fields.help: Thinking level, from the CLI's own vocabulary. Which values exist (and whether the CLI has the seam at all) is the backend's answer — `agent_cli_knobs` — never a list mirrored here. Empty = the CLI's default.

fields.name: context
fields.help: Context-window variant, e.g. "1m". Same ownership as `effort`: the backend states what is deliverable. Empty = the model's own window.

edge.title: Connection
edge.help: One advisory hand-off. The file may write `to:` as a list to fan out; each target reads as one connection.

fields.name: from
fields.help: The block this hand-off leaves.

fields.name: to
fields.help: The block it points at. A list here (`to: [rev-a, rev-b]`) is a fan-out — one connection per target.

gate.title: Merge gate
gate.help: What must be recorded before loomux will let `gh pr merge` through.

fields.name: require
fields.help: `all-pass` = every named reviewer recorded PASS. `threshold` = at least N of them did.

fields.name: threshold
fields.help: How many passing reviews a `threshold` gate needs. Meaningless — and refused above the reviewer count — otherwise.

fields.name: reviewers
fields.help: The blocks whose verdict the gate waits for. Each must be a reviewer-kind block, or the gate could never open.

fields.name: also
fields.help: Extra conditions, e.g. "ci-green", "body-unchanged". The backend owns what each one means.

intake.title: Intake
intake.help: Where autonomous work comes from. Inert vocabulary plus an adapter chosen from a fixed set — there is deliberately no spelling here that can weaken the human merge gate.

fields.name: source
fields.help: Which adapter supplies work. `github-labels` polls issues by label (today's wired behavior); `board` and `none` are schema-reserved.

fields.name: labels
fields.help: This repo's label spellings. Declare one and the other three keep their built-in defaults.

intake.labels.title: Intake labels
intake.labels.help: The label vocabulary intake matches on. Letters, digits, '-' and '_' — a label that would need rewriting is refused, never silently changed.

fields.name: ready
fields.help: "Build this." — groomed, go.

fields.name: investigate
fields.help: "Look, don't build." — research only; findings go on the issue.

fields.name: owned
fields.help: "Mine." — an orchestrator has taken this issue.

fields.name: prototype
fields.help: "Build it for a demo." — feedback-gated work.

merge_queue.title: Merge queue
merge_queue.help: Policy for the bisecting merge queue (#581). Policy, not mechanism: nothing here names a branch or a verification command — the queue observes the repo's own CI, and the target comes from the enqueued PR's live base.

fields.name: enabled
fields.help: Off by default. Off means every queue path is unreachable, not merely unused.

fields.name: max_batch
fields.help: How many approved sub-PRs one speculative batch may carry. At 3, a red batch costs at most 2 extra CI runs to attribute.

fields.name: checks_timeout_minutes
fields.help: Backstop on waiting for a batch's checks, so a repo with no checks attached surfaces as unverifiable instead of pending in silence. Clamped into range rather than refused.

resource.title: Lock resource
resource.help: One named thing agents must take turns on. Restrict-only: the whole schema is two numbers, and the worst a declaration can do is make an agent wait.

fields.name: slots
fields.help: How many agents may hold it at once. 1 (the default) is a mutex; a repo that wants a semaphore says so.

fields.name: max_hold_minutes
fields.help: How long one hold may last before the sweep reclaims it — the bound that keeps a crashed holder from parking the resource forever.
